reason: Driven at 1440x960 and 1024x800 on owner-flight and desk, the behaviour is exactly as described but the reading of it is wrong. At rest the pair is 'TODAY IS 16 JULY' / 'Nothing is planned until 1 August.'; scrolled it becomes '8 August · 23 days away', then '5 September · 51 days away', and it returns to the rest sentence at scrollY 0 (round 7's live-derivation fix holds; no stale snapshot). (1) The claimed contradiction does not exist arithmetically. Every scrolled readout states its distance FROM the label's date: 16 July + 23 = 8 August, + 51 = 5 September, + 65 = 19 September (1024 width). The label is not announcing a rival date, it is the origin the second half of the line is measured from - without it '51 days away' is unanchored, which is the exact defect round 7 refuted 'deleting one of the two statements of today' to protect. The label governs the line more tightly when scrolled than at rest. (2) The at-rest 'consequence' relationship the finding contrasts against is not there either. 'Nothing is planned until 1 August.' is a complete independent sentence with its own subject and verb; it is not a value under a label. So the register does not change on scroll - both states are the same construction: today, then the nearest thing in the plan expressed relative to today. (3) The label is not a section head. It is a caption on the indigo .b-todayRule immediately above it, and .b-who ('MARA & FINN', the project name) shares the identical uppercase-mono spec, so 'uppercase mono = section head that must name what is below it' is the refuter's extrapolation, not a rule this file follows. (4) The fix makes it worse, measurably. .b-stick on owner-flight holds horizon(), then .b-editHost, then .b-undoHome. I injected the proposed extra label line and measured: the docked editor and the undo bar both move down 24px (editHost 597 -> 621, undoHome 1156 -> 1180; stick height 925 -> 949 on owner-editing). Because the fix inserts on scroll and removes on scroll-back, the open editing panel and the one control that takes a change back would jog 24px each way while the owner scrolls - the same class round 7 refuted with 'the steppers do NOT hold still under scroll'. (5) The fix also reintroduces a paid-for defect: a second uppercase-mono string at byte-identical spec ('set at var(--fore-62) like the label beside it') sitting directly beside the first, which is precisely the twenty-seven-of-thirty-two collapse b.css spent a round separating. And 'IN VIEW' is viewport chrome jargon in the most emotional block on the screen, for an audience defined as someone who has never used a tool like this. (6) Minor but telling: the prescribed micro() helper lives in render-core.js and emits <span class="micro">, a class with no rule anywhere in b.css, a.css, c.css or shell.css - the fix was not checked against the code it names.
